How to Write a HVAC Technician Resume

An HVAC technician resume should name the systems, refrigerants, building types, controls, service volume, diagnostic work, energy results, and safety credentials relevant to the target employer.

Example

HVAC Technician resume summary

Use this as a pattern for level, scope, specialty, and evidence. Do not copy facts that are not yours.

HVAC technician with 7 years of commercial service experience across rooftop units, split systems, boilers, and building controls. Improved first-visit resolution and reduced repeat calls through structured diagnostics.
Recommended order

How to structure the resume

  1. Contact details and target title. Use the normal title from the job posting and provide working contact links.
  2. Focused summary. Establish your level, setting, specialty, and one representative outcome.
  3. Recent relevant experience. Use reverse chronological order and give the most space to work that resembles the target role.
  4. Role-specific skills. Keep a scannable list, then prove the important skills in bullets.
  5. Education and credentials. Place EPA Section 608, state licenses, NATE, OSHA, refrigerant, controls, and manufacturer certifications near the top when current and relevant.
Use only what you can support

Skills to include

Match the employer's terminology when it accurately describes your experience.

  • HVAC diagnostics
  • Preventive maintenance
  • Refrigeration
  • Electrical troubleshooting
  • Building controls
  • Air balancing
  • Customer service
  • Safety
Evidence ideas

Useful metrics for a hvac technician resume

Numbers should clarify scope or change. They do not need to be revenue figures.

Service

Calls, first-time fix, callbacks, or response time

Equipment

Tonnage, units, sites, or system types

Efficiency

Energy, runtime, downtime, or maintenance completion

Writing patterns

HVAC Technician resume bullet examples

Adapt the action, context, and result to your own verified work.

  • Raised first-visit resolution to 87% across commercial service calls.
  • Maintained HVAC systems at 32 retail and office locations.
  • Diagnosed a controls fault that reduced repeated comfort complaints.
  • Completed preventive-maintenance routes with accurate readings and follow-up recommendations.
Look for

Strong signals

  • Diagnostic depth
  • System experience
  • Service reliability
  • Safe compliance
Avoid

Common mistakes

  • No EPA or license status
  • A parts list without diagnostic reasoning
  • Mixing residential and commercial claims without context
  • Omitting electrical and safety practices

Questions, answered

Resume FAQ

What should a hvac technician resume include?

Lead with diagnostic depth, show relevant hvac diagnostics experience in context, and use achievement bullets that explain scope and outcome.

What skills belong on a hvac technician resume?

Prioritize skills from the target job that you can prove in experience, projects, education, or credentials. Useful examples include hvac diagnostics, preventive maintenance, refrigeration, electrical troubleshooting.

Can I use the example numbers and bullet points?

No. The examples demonstrate structure and specificity. Replace every action, number, tool, and result with evidence that is true for your own work.

Which resume format should I use?

Reverse chronological format works for most candidates. Use a combination format when projects or transferable skills need more emphasis, but keep dates and work history clear.
